description:
Freeze the logical candidate portfolio, measure the XOR unroll portfolio and the consumer-specific dispatch candidate, and select the logical-buffer production outcome.

## Background

**0064b0a2 — Freeze the logical candidate portfolio.** Turn the current logical baselines and profiles into a bounded portfolio for the XOR unroll and consumer-specific dispatch experiments before candidate samples are collected. The portfolio names a finite unroll-factor family and at most one measured unhoisted consumer with a materially different call contract. It keeps the 64-word generic-hoist no-win and already-hoisted algorithm loops out of the search. ISA-L remains an external comparison under its qualified symbol and adapter contract.

**42a22210 — Measure the XOR unroll portfolio.** Implement only the predeclared private unroll variants and compare them with the established scalar and selected SIMD XOR kernels. Unroll factors are experimental arms, not production routes. The study uses the frozen cell family and complexity budget, compiles intrinsic-bearing variants with Rust 1.95, retains runtime feature gating plus the tested scalar fallback, and keeps unsafe code inside `gf2-kernels-simd`. Every new unsafe boundary requires an explicit safety contract.

**80ed6e9f — Measure the consumer-specific dispatch candidate.** Implement the one predeclared consumer-specific dispatch experiment and compare it with the current public-call path. The experiment targets a measured unhoisted consumer and must have a materially different call contract from the preserved 64-word generic-hoist no-win. Already-hoisted M4RM, RREF, Gauss, Strassen, and degenerate multiply loops remain controls, not migration targets.

**a5f29ae5 — Select the logical-buffer production outcome.** Apply the frozen adoption rules to the unroll, consumer-specific dispatch, and ISA-L comparison evidence, producing one auditable logical-buffer outcome. Selection uses confidence-bound whole-consumer benefit, equivalence non-regression, maintenance complexity, and declared dispatch domain. External throughput alone cannot select a production route, and the established implementation remains when no candidate qualifies.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: (0064b0a2 REQ-01) The portfolio names each exact logical candidate, target cells, rationale from current profiles, implementation complexity budget, comparison family, and stop condition before candidate measurement.
- [hard] REQ-02: (0064b0a2 REQ-02) A missing profile signal is recorded as a no-candidate outcome rather than replaced with an unmeasured optimization, and the preserved generic-hoist no-win remains excluded.
- [hard] REQ-03: (0064b0a2 REQ-03) Candidate scopes use the canonical logical-buffer and dispatch authority without pre-authorizing a production change.

- [hard] REQ-04: (42a22210 REQ-01) Each predeclared unroll arm has shared equivalence coverage for aligned, offset, empty, and 0/1/63/64/65 boundary cases before timed measurement.
- [hard] REQ-05: (42a22210 REQ-02) The receipt reports raw samples, adjusted confidence bounds, equivalence results, complexity accounting, annotated release assembly, and profile explanations for each arm.
- [hard] REQ-06: (42a22210 REQ-03) No candidate enters production in this issue, and negative or inconclusive arms remain preserved.
- [hard] REQ-07: (42a22210 REQ-04) Every new unsafe boundary is isolated to `gf2-kernels-simd` and carries an explicit safety contract covering pointer validity, slice lengths, aliasing, required target features, runtime gating, and scalar fallback reachability.

- [hard] REQ-08: (80ed6e9f REQ-01) The candidate is bounded to the profile-identified unhoisted consumer and has shared semantic coverage across selected worker counts, fallbacks, offset views, and boundary sizes.
- [hard] REQ-09: (80ed6e9f REQ-02) The receipt reports dispatch-inclusive whole-consumer samples, adjusted confidence bounds, equivalence results, complexity accounting, assembly, and profile attribution.
- [hard] REQ-10: (80ed6e9f REQ-03) The 64-word generic-hoist no-win remains unchanged, no production helper lands in this issue, and negative evidence is retained.

- [hard] REQ-11: (a5f29ae5 REQ-01) The decision evaluates each candidate against the predeclared worthwhile-effect, equivalence-margin, complexity, and multiple-comparison rules using only confirmatory evidence.
- [hard] REQ-12: (a5f29ae5 REQ-02) At most one bounded production change is selected with its exact dispatch domain and required before/after cells, or a no-adoption outcome preserves the established route and all losing evidence.
- [hard] REQ-13: (a5f29ae5 REQ-03) The preserved 64-word generic-hoist no-win is not reopened without a materially different consumer contract.

## Notes

Merged in session 19 (invoker ruling, 2026-09-17) from 0064b0a2, 42a22210, 80ed6e9f, a5f29ae5; every criterion above is verbatim from its source issue and none is loosened. The merged task runs each stage in its source order (freeze committed before any trial, pilot before confirmation) and follows dev/active/1a379447-zen3-cpu-performance/worker-brief.md and protocol v4.

0064b0a2: This is an experimental selection contract, not a production adoption decision.

42a22210: Private experimental symbols must not create a second public dispatch abstraction.

80ed6e9f: The experiment may bind an existing resolver privately; it must not introduce a parallel dispatch authority.

a5f29ae5: The decision record is the only authority consumed by the conditional adoption task.
title: Freeze, measure and select the logical-buffer candidates
